title: Identifying and Targeting the Causal Root of LLM Lean Proof Failure: Wrong Induction Structure

original_idea.body:
# Identifying and Targeting the Causal Root of LLM Lean Proof Failure: Wrong Induction Structure

**Problem:** A significant fraction of Lean 4 proof failures appear to involve choosing the wrong induction hypothesis or induction variable. Whether 'wrong induction structure' is the single most common root cause of LLM proof failures — and whether targeted hints address it — is not tested.

**Direction:** Analyze 100 LLM Lean 4 failures. Classify by root cause using a structured taxonomy. Test whether 'wrong induction structure' is most common. For that class, implement a single targeted intervention: system prompt addition that describes how to select induction variables. Measure improvement.

**Why it matters:** If one failure mode dominates, fixing it provides the largest marginal improvement in compilation rate. A targeted, narrow intervention (vs. broad architecture redesign) is more tractable for student researchers and more actionable for tool developers.

**Relevant context:** Induction is the most common proof technique in Lean 4 for recursive programs. Human Lean novices consistently struggle with induction hypothesis selection. Whether LLMs share this failure is assumed but not measured.
